output.name: Vorél — the Crooked Wedge
output.myth: Each autumn the grey geese go south in a wedge, and the old women say the wedge is Kael's net. Kael cast it over the sea for a fallen star. He never caught one, but the cords stayed in the sky. Tavo the Gale raised a sea over the Leeward Reach and drove Hasken's three boats past the last rock, and they never came home. Hesk counted them at the pole and wound a line for each. Ennu had shown those men how to set their sails in a wedge, so the drowned gave the shape to the geese. The Ferry Sail, Halan, lies off to the south-west, square as Ennu sewed it, for the crossing those boats made each spring. Solva, the Torn Sleeve, hangs a fist below the wedge's head, torn where Tavo laughed at it. The lead bird points the way the boats should have come home. Its wedge is always a little crooked, because Hasken's youngest steered badly, and the goose has never forgiven him. If you see the wedge over the water, mend your net, count your children, and do not watch too long. The sky keeps what looks at it.
output.finding: From Solva, the Torn Sleeve, look a fist and a bit to the north, and you will find the wedge's lead bird over the water.
